messages:
maya_cs: Quick morning check — cutting over Garnet private VPC tomorrow 09:00 PT. Need final confirmation on networking rules, IAM role mapping, KMS key rotation window, and audit log forwarding. Any blockers?
alex_ops: thanks — team is ready on our side but two open items: 1) our infra team flagged potential CIDR overlap if Redwood uses 10.2.0.0/16 for the private gateway. 2) audit logs need to go to our Splunk forwarder (hosted in us-west-2) — do you support TLS forwarder IP allowlist? :thinking:
priya_net: Re: CIDR — we can use 10.8.0.0/16 for Garnet to avoid overlap. Can confirm route table entries and peering config. For Splunk, we support whitelist by IP and by FQDN for TLS endpoints; preference is FQDN + mTLS if you enable it.
liam_se: IAM & KMS notes: we'll create a cross-account role with a trust policy allowing the customer's provisioning role. Example trust snippet:

```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/garnet-provisioner"},
    "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
  }]
}
```

KMS: we need the key ARN and whether rotation is customer-managed. If you want us to create a key in your account, we'll request kms:CreateKey permission during provisioning.
alex_ops: we will hand over a customer-managed CMK ARN. Rotation is on our side monthly, not automatic. Also Splunk endpoint is logs.garnet.ops.example.com (TLS); forwarding IPs are dynamic behind CloudFront — prefer FQDN allowlist + mTLS.
priya_net: ok noted. For firewall/nat — outbound egress to Splunk port 6514 TCP. We'll include a rule example for your firewall team:

```
allow tcp 10.8.0.0/16 -> logs.garnet.ops.example.com:6514
allow tcp 10.8.0.0/16 -> 0.0.0.0/0:443 (for package updates; restricted)
```

If your infra requires static IPs, we can provide a small egress NAT pool (x.x.x.100-104) for allowlisting.
maya_cs: Action items summary:
- alex_ops: confirm acceptance of 10.8.0.0/16 CIDR and provide CMK ARN + Splunk FQDN/mTLS cert thumbprint (if available) — owner: alex_ops — due: today EOD.
- priya_net: prepare route table + NAT egress pool and post exact IPs in this thread — owner: priya_net — due: today 17:00 PT.
- liam_se: prepare IAM trust policy document and KMS permission list; prep runbook for key rotation handover — owner: liam_se — due: today 18:00 PT.

Can we also do a 30-min cutover dry-run 1 hour before actual cutover? :calendar:
alex_ops: yes to dry-run. We'll have our infra lead (Jordan) join. One more ask: if the KMS key rotates mid-cutover, what's your fallback? :warning:
liam_se: fallback: if key becomes unavailable we fail gracefully and rollback interface to hosted model variant (no access to private data). We also have a cached-encryption-window for ephemeral tokens (30 min). We'll document this in the runbook.
maya_cs: noting risk: KMS rotation mismatches are a medium renewal risk if not coordinated. If we hit >24h delay because of key issues, I'll flag renewal CSM and propose a short professional services engagement to finish cutover.
priya_net: posted NAT egress IPs: [54.213.101.45, 54.213.101.46, 54.213.101.47] — please confirm allowlist. Also uploaded VPC route table export to S3: https://redwood-internal.s3.amazonaws.com/garnet/routes-1718214321.json :link:
alex_ops: confirmed CIDR + NAT IPs, forwarding cert thumbprint attached (sha256: abcd1234...). Jordan will join dry-run. :thumbsup:
maya_cs: perfect — I'll schedule the 30-min dry-run at 08:00 PT and cutover at 09:00 PT. I'll ping #eng-onsite if anything surprises us. Thanks everyone — short sync after cutover to capture feedback.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: garnet-privnet-cutover at 2024-06-18T09:00:00-07:00 (dry-run 2024-06-18T08:00:00-07:00). Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/garnet/cutover_v1 — started precheck 1718218000, precheck status: OK.
